title: Call Recording Storage Cost: The Line Item That Grows Every Month
desc: Recording a call costs $0.0025 a minute once. Storing it costs $0.0005 a minute every month. The compounding math for Twilio and GoHighLevel sub-accounts.
keywords: call recording storage cost, twilio recording storage pricing, gohighlevel call recording storage, lc phone recording storage, call recording cost per minute
cta: Want your telephony costs audited across sub-accounts?
body:
September 24, 2026. Twilio began moving accounts onto an updated Voice Recording Storage billing system on September 17. The price is unchanged, Twilio says, but daily usage metrics in the Console and the Usage API may shift because the new system is more accurate. It is a good moment to look at the line itself, because recording storage is the one telephony charge that keeps growing while your call volume stays flat. For an agency with call recording switched on across client sub-accounts, it is a cost that compounds quietly for years.

What recording and storage cost today

  1. Twilio's United States voice pricing lists call recording at $0.0025 per minute and storage at $0.0005 per minute per month.
  2. Storage has volume tiers: $0.00050 for the first 5 million minutes a month, $0.00025 for the next 10 million, and $0.00015 above 15 million.
  3. HighLevel's phone system pricing guide charges the same $0.0025 per minute to record and $0.0005 per minute per month to store, billed daily per sub-account, plus $0.024 per minute for call transcription.
  4. Twilio's help centre says it keeps recordings until you remove them, and rounds each recording up to the next minute, so three five-second recordings bill as three minutes.
  5. Storage fees apply only to recordings kept in Twilio's cloud. Recordings sent to external storage such as AWS S3 are billed by that provider instead.

Why the storage line compounds

You pay to record a minute once. You pay to store it every month. At these rates a recording kept for five months has cost as much to store as it cost to make, and one kept for about 25 months has cost more to store than HighLevel's $0.0126 outbound US calling minute.

Take one client recording 100 minutes of calls a day, about 3,000 a month, and apply the daily running-total method Twilio documents, which reproduces Twilio's own worked example to the cent. The recording fee is a flat $7.50 a month. The storage bill is $0.78 in month one, $8.28 in month six, when it passes the recording fee, $17.28 in month twelve and $35.27 in month twenty-four. Storage over the first year totals $108.30, more than the $90 spent recording. Spread that pattern across 30 client sub-accounts and storage alone reaches about $518 a month after one year and $1,058 a month after two, with no change in call volume.

What it means for operators

  1. Set a retention period. HighLevel's guide points to Settings, Phone Numbers, Advanced Settings, Voice Calls, Call Recording to delete older recordings automatically. With 90-day retention, the same client holds a steady 9,000 stored minutes, about $4.50 a month, instead of a bill that climbs every month.
  2. Check what you are obliged to keep first. Some clients, contracts and regulated industries require recordings to be retained, and Twilio's own help article reminds you that consent-to-record laws such as California's apply. If you must keep them, export to storage you control rather than paying cloud storage rates indefinitely.
  3. Put storage in the rebilled usage. If you resell phone service to clients, this line belongs in what they pay, not in your margin. It is one of the details we build into white-label GoHighLevel SaaS setups, because it is invisible at launch and material by year two.
  4. Watch short-call volume. Per-recording rounding means voicemail drops and missed-call recordings bill a full minute each.

Transcription is the other recurring question on the same calls, and we cover it in what AI transcription costs per hour. If you want an audit of recording and telephony settings across your sub-accounts, our GoHighLevel services team does it as a fixed-scope job.
faqs: How much does call recording storage cost on Twilio?

Twilio's United States pricing lists recording storage at $0.0005 per minute per month for the first 5 million minutes, falling to $0.00025 for the next 10 million and $0.00015 above 15 million. Recording itself is a separate $0.0025 per minute.
Does GoHighLevel charge for call recording storage?

Yes. HighLevel's phone system pricing guide lists call recording storage at $0.0005 per minute per month, billed daily per sub-account, on top of $0.0025 per minute to record. Older recordings keep incurring the charge until they are deleted.
How do I stop paying for old call recordings in GoHighLevel?

HighLevel's guide says to go to Settings, Phone Numbers, Advanced Settings, Voice Calls, Call Recording and set older recordings to delete automatically, or set the deletion period to one day and disable recording for future calls. Check any legal or contractual retention duty first.
Why does a short call bill a full minute of storage?
Twilio rounds each recording up to the next minute for storage, so three recordings of five seconds each count as three minutes, not fifteen seconds.
